categories.name: It works
categories.notes: Build 5/5: 0 errors, 0 warnings. Front page 10/10: / returns 200 and is the blog home. It lists both posts with working links, and each card has an image, a date, the title, an excerpt and a 'Read field note' link. Posts 10/10: both render the hero and rich-text blocks fully with no errors. Images 5/5: the three provided Unsplash photos were imported into the 'MCP Blog' media folder and served through signed GetCropUrl URLs (5/5 load). Domain/publish 5/5: domain '/' (en-US) is set on the 'MCP Field Notes' page and all content is published.

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: Folders 8/8: heroBlock, richTextBlock and blogPostListBlock are elements in Blocks, blogHomePage and blogPostPage are in Pages, and siteRoot is in Repositories. Block grid 4/7: the grid is on both page types, but the block set is only hero, rich text and post listing. There is no standalone image block or quote block, and each post is a hero plus ONE rich-text block holding the whole article (headings, quote and list inside the RTE), which is the weak model. Structure 5/5: siteRoot is the only root type, siteRoot -> blogHomePage -> blogPostPage, templates are assigned, aliases are camelCase, and 'Blog Block Grid' is in /Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid. Hygiene 2/5: blogPostPage has no metadata properties. The listing card's excerpt and image are taken from the post's first heroBlock, and its date is CreateDate, so there is no editable publish date, excerpt or listing image. There are no compositions and no duplicated or orphaned types.

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: Rendering 7/7: blogHomePage.cshtml and blogPostPage.cshtml just call Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "blocks"), and the scaffold's blockgrid partials are unchanged. Adapters 6/6: Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/{heroBlock,richTextBlock,blogPostListBlock}.cshtml each take BlockGridItem<T>, map to a plain model and call Component.InvokeAsync, with no markup. The listing adapter does its child query there, which is acceptable. ViewComponents 7/7: Hero, RichText and BlogPostList each render Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml. The plain models live in Models/Blocks and Models/Blog, and the component views have no Umbraco dependencies. Conventions 5/5: Program.cs and appsettings.json are untouched, there are no migrations, and there is no .cs file in the Models root. It uses friendly extensions and GetCropUrl, and styling is Tailwind built to wwwroot/dist/site.css.

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Posts 4/6: two on-topic, accurate posts ('Why MCP Makes Software Feel Alive', 'Local MCP Is a Developer Superpower'), each with about 6-7 paragraphs, h2 sections, a blockquote or bullet list. They are substantive but leaning self-referential ('this site was built through MCP'). Each post is a single rich-text block with one image (the hero), so the content is not spread over several blocks. Look 4/4: polished dark hero with a tilted framed image and photo credit, a clean two-card listing with image, date, title and excerpt, a readable centred post column with styled headings and blockquote, and a consistent header and footer.

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: Channel 3/3: schema, media and content were built only through Umbraco MCP (38 calls, 20 writes), with no browser, Management API, uSync, DB or migration use. Razor was written after a restart and there are no order warnings. No memory, results/ or tests/ access. Its only outside read was the Umbraco.Core XML docs in the NuGet cache, used to look up the API, which doesn't warrant a deduction. Report 2/2: the final report is accurate and 'no known issues' holds up.

summary: A polished MCP-built blog ('MCP Field Notes'): hero + post-listing front page and two substantive posts, with a textbook adapter -> ViewComponent architecture and everything working. The weak point is the content model: posts are a hero plus one rich-text block, with no image block and no real date/excerpt/listing-image properties.
strengths: All 43 automated checks pass; clean build with 0 warnings
Textbook rendering chain: GetBlockGridHtmlAsync -> markup-free adapters -> ViewComponents with plain models
Provided Unsplash photos imported into a media folder and served via signed GetCropUrl
Attractive, coherent Tailwind design with a proper card listing
Built strictly through MCP with an accurate final report

issues.text: Each post is a heroBlock plus one richTextBlock holding the entire article. There is no image or quote block, so the block set is thin (Blog Block Grid data type; documents /why-mcp-makes-software-feel-alive/, /local-mcp-is-a-developer-superpower/).

blogPostPage has no date, excerpt or listing-image properties. The card excerpt and image are pulled from the post's first heroBlock and the date is CreateDate (Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/blogPostListBlock.cshtml).
Each post has only one image (the hero), and the post copy leans self-referential about how this site was built.
